Keywords: trunk based development main short-lived branches feature flags CI
Description: All developers commit frequently to a single main branch (trunk). Feature branches live for <1 day. Feature flags control rollout. Requires strong CI.
When to Use: High-velocity teams with strong CI/CD — enables continuous deployment to production
Command Example:
# Short-lived feature branch (same day merge)
git switch -c feature/add-trusted-host-middleware
# ... make changes, commit
git push -u origin feature/add-trusted-host-middleware
# Open PR -> must pass CI -> squash merge -> delete branch
# Main is always deployable -- no long-lived branches
Gotchas: Requires mature CI and feature flag infrastructure. Without fast automated tests trunk-based development leads to broken deployments.

Keywords: gitflow feature develop release hotfix tags long-lived Vincent Vincent Driessen
Description: Gitflow uses long-lived main and develop branches with feature release and hotfix branches. Releases are tagged on main. Developed by Vincent Driessen.
When to Use: Projects with scheduled releases and multiple parallel versions — common in library and product development
Command Example:
# Initialize gitflow
git flow init

# Start a feature
git flow feature start add-cors-middleware

# Finish a feature (merges to develop)
git flow feature finish add-cors-middleware

# Create a release
git flow release start 2.1.0
git flow release finish 2.1.0  # merges to main + develop + tags
Gotchas: Gitflow adds overhead for small teams. Long-lived branches increase merge conflict risk. Modern teams often prefer trunk-based for faster iteration.

Keywords: semver version tag release major minor patch annotated git tag
Description: Use semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) for release tags. Create annotated tags on main for releases. Push tags separately from commits.
When to Use: Every production release — semver communicates breaking changes (major) features (minor) or fixes (patch)
Command Example:
# Create an annotated release tag
git tag -a v2.1.0 -m 'Release v2.1.0
- Add CORSMiddleware (configurable via env)
- Add bare Exception guard
- Add semaphore to list_miners'

# Push tag to remote
git push origin v2.1.0

# List all tags sorted by version
git tag --sort=version:refname

# Delete a wrong tag
git tag -d v2.1.0-draft
git push origin --delete v2.1.0-draft
Gotchas: Lightweight tags (git tag v2.1.0) have no message or tagger info. Always use annotated tags (-a) for releases. Semver pre-releases: v2.1.0-rc.1.

Keywords: PR pull request review merge branch fork GitHub GitLab code review
Description: Open a Pull Request (PR) from a feature branch to main/develop. Require code review CI checks and approval before merging. The standard collaborative workflow.
When to Use: Any change to a shared codebase — PRs enable code review, discussion, and CI gating
Command Example:
# 1. Branch from main
git switch -c feature/GH-42-add-exception-guard

# 2. Commit changes with conventional messages
git commit -m 'feat(errors): add bare Exception catch-all handler'

# 3. Push and open PR
git push -u origin feature/GH-42-add-exception-guard
# -> Open PR on GitHub -> request review -> CI must pass -> squash merge

# 4. After merge — delete remote branch
git push origin --delete feature/GH-42-add-exception-guard
git branch -d feature/GH-42-add-exception-guard
Gotchas: PR titles should follow Conventional Commits format — many platforms use it for automated changelogs. Keep PRs small (<400 lines) for better review quality.

Keywords: github flow simple main feature branch CI continuous deploy
Description: GitHub Flow is a simplified workflow: branch from main. work. open PR. review. merge to main. Deploy immediately. No develop branch or release branches.
When to Use: Small teams deploying continuously — simpler than Gitflow with fewer branch types
Command Example:
# GitHub Flow in 5 steps:
# 1. Branch from main
git switch -c feature/add-semaphore-to-miners

# 2. Make atomic commits
git commit -m 'perf(miners): cap RPC fan-out at 10 concurrent calls'

# 3. Push often
git push origin feature/add-semaphore-to-miners

# 4. Open PR, get review, CI must pass

# 5. Merge to main -> deploy
# (use squash merge for clean history)
Gotchas: GitHub Flow assumes you deploy from main immediately. If you need staging or release branches you need a more complex workflow.

Keywords: changelog automated conventional commits semantic-release git log
Description: Generate changelogs automatically from commit history using tools like conventional-changelog or semantic-release based on Conventional Commits messages.
When to Use: Before every release — saves manual changelog writing and keeps it accurate
Command Example:
# Install conventional-changelog
npm install -g conventional-changelog-cli

# Generate CHANGELOG.md from last tag to HEAD
conventional-changelog -p angular -i CHANGELOG.md -s

# Or use semantic-release for fully automated versioning + changelog
npx semantic-release

# Manual: extract from git log
git log v1.0.0..HEAD --pretty='- %s' | grep '^- feat\|^- fix'
Gotchas: Requires ALL commits to follow Conventional Commits format — one non-compliant commit breaks categorization. Enforce with commit-msg hook.

Keywords: release branch stabilize hotfix fix freeze merge back
Description: Create a release branch from develop when stabilizing a release. Only bug fixes go into the release branch. After release merge back to main and develop.
When to Use: Projects that need a stabilization period before release — common in products with QA cycles
Command Example:
# Cut a release branch
git switch -c release/2.1.0 develop

# Only bug fixes during stabilization
git commit -m 'fix(auth): handle expired token edge case'

# Finish release: merge to main and develop
git switch main
git merge --no-ff release/2.1.0
git tag -a v2.1.0 -m 'Release v2.1.0'

git switch develop
git merge --no-ff release/2.1.0
git branch -d release/2.1.0
Gotchas: Release branches require discipline — no features allowed. Feature freeze must be enforced through PR rules. Complex for small teams.

Keywords: gitignore ignore patterns exclude files secrets env build artifacts tracked
Description: Configure .gitignore to exclude files that should never be tracked: secrets env files build output compiled binaries logs. Use .gitignore.io to generate templates.
When to Use: Every new project — set up .gitignore before the first commit to avoid tracking secrets
Command Example:
# Common patterns for a Python web project
# .gitignore
__pycache__/
*.pyc
*.pyo
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
*.egg-info/
dist/
build/
.pytest_cache/
.mypy_cache/
.ruff_cache/
*.log

# Generate at gitignore.io
curl -L https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/python,fastapi > .gitignore

# Remove already-tracked files that should be ignored
git rm --cached path/to/secret.env
Gotchas: If secrets are accidentally committed they are in history FOREVER — even if removed. You MUST rotate all leaked secrets immediately and consider the breach permanent.
